task.title: Clear the two chronic e2e manifest reds blocking the pin and three landings
task.description:
- **e2e.manifest_c_programs (206 retained logs) and e2e.manifest_backend_parity_c (77) ARE THE LAST TWO OF THE FIVE CHRONIC MAIN REDS. check.lint_checks and test.regular_crates cleared on their own; check.portability_paths was cleared with all 8 legacy fixture files re-hashed byte-identical and nothing weakened, retired or deleted.**
- **THEY BLOCK MORE THAN ONE THING: the reverie pin bump, hermit 3066, and at least one further landing all wait on this same pair. That is why they are worth attacking directly rather than routing around.**
- **THE MEASURED CONTEXT, so the scale is checkable: RUN 1866 at 80ce2ee94689 executed 269 of 270 nodes in 34m17s at -j 16 with 3 failures. Before PR 3080 the same profile managed 14 executed, 1 failed, 256 skipped and ZERO tests.**
- ⚠️ **DO NOT CLEAR THESE BY RELAXING AN ASSERTION, RETIRING A CELL OR WIDENING A TOLERANCE. They have survived long enough that the convenient fix will look reasonable, and a node that passes because it stopped looking is worse than one that is red. If a cell encodes an obsolete expectation, say so with evidence rather than deleting it.**
- ⚠️ **206 AND 77 RETAINED LOGS ARE AN ASSET RATHER THAN A BURDEN — that is a large evidence base for establishing whether these are one cause or two. Establish that before fixing either; this project has repeatedly found cells grouped by name that had different causes, and cells with different names that shared one.**
- **ENVIRONMENT HAZARD HIT THREE TIMES TONIGHT BY THE SAME LANE: a fresh worktree has no submodules, so a rust-script test invocation there fails for a reason unrelated to the code under test.**
- **Verify:** both nodes pass at current main in a full-profile run, with the cause named for each and an explicit statement that no assertion, tolerance, cell or case was weakened.

notes.content:
THREE CAUSES, NOT ONE AND NOT TWO -- AND THE NODE GROUPING DOES NOT MATCH THE
CAUSE GROUPING. Established before attempting any fix, as the task required.
Nothing was changed: no assertion, tolerance, cell or case was weakened,
retired, widened or deleted. This note is analysis only.

SCALE FIRST, because the two nodes are nothing alike:

  e2e.manifest_c_programs         431 PASS,   3 FAIL lines,  2 failing cells
  e2e.manifest_backend_parity_c   103 PASS, 344 FAIL lines, 99 failing cells

c-programs is 99.5% green with two isolated cells. backend-parity-c is roughly
half its cells failing. Treating them as a matched pair of "chronic e2e reds"
conceals that.

=== CAUSE 1: backend-parity-c, ALL 99 CELLS, ONE MECHANISM ===

Every failing cell carries the IDENTICAL signature
[turn=1 vns=1767225600000500000 rec=10], 144 occurrences for kvm plus 192 for
liteinst. Same turn, same virtual time, same record index, across unrelated
guests. That is a property of the BACKENDS, not of any guest.

BOTH SIDES ARE INTERNALLY DETERMINISTIC. Sampled 76 self-verification reports:
76/76 verdict=matched, bitwise_parity=true. Nothing here is nondeterministic.
The failure is purely the CROSS-BACKEND comparison.

THE MECHANISM, measured directly from the retained logs rather than inferred.
For eight unrelated cells, candidate vs parity-reference `inbound rdtsc` counts:

  aio-refusal              kvm  candidate 0/96   reference 10/106
  append-pwrite            kvm  candidate 0/133  reference 10/151
  bind-getsockname         kvm  candidate 0/99   reference 10/109
  cachestat-refusal        kvm  candidate 0/113  reference 10/131
  child-subreaper-refusal  kvm  candidate 0/92   reference 10/102
  close-range-fds          kvm  candidate 0/126  reference 10/144
  copy-file-range-refusal  kvm  candidate 0/128  reference 10/142
  cpu-virtualization       kvm  candidate 0/93   reference 10/103
                                (rdtsc / total INFO detcore records)

The ptrace reference emits exactly TEN `inbound rdtsc` Detcore INFO records in
every cell; kvm emits ZERO. liteinst emits a different number again (12 in the
cell inspected). These are backend-exclusive records: ptrace intercepts rdtsc
and logs it with the new logical time, KVM does not surface it the same way.

The comparison is CrossBackendDetcoreV1 with
included_detlog_kinds = ["syscall","syscall_result","other"], and its own
contract in hermit-cli/src/logdiff_report.rs states: "Raw record populations can
differ across backends; the selected streams of a match cannot", enforced as
records.compared == min(available_left, available_right). The backend-exclusive
rdtsc records are admitted into the selected envelope, so the two aligned
streams desynchronise at the first one and every cell reports divergence at
record 10.

I DID NOT FIX THIS, DELIBERATELY. The convenient fix -- excluding rdtsc from the
shared envelope -- is exactly the goalpost move the task forbids, and it is not
a lint-level decision: rdtsc feeds DetTime and logical time, so what belongs in
a cross-backend INFO envelope is a determinism-semantics question. This
repository has a deterministic-scheduling-review procedure for precisely that
class. Whether the right answer is (a) narrow the envelope so backend-exclusive
interception records are not compared, or (b) make the backends agree on what
they log, is a design decision with a determinism argument attached, and one
lane clearing a red should not make it silently for 99 cells.

=== CAUSE 2: c-programs / netlink-autobind-generic (verify/sabre) ===

[turn=2 vns=1767225600001773500 rec=10] canonical verification did not match:
verified=false. Distinct from cause 1: different node, different backend
(sabre), different turn, and it is a canonical self-verification mismatch rather
than a cross-backend envelope misalignment. Consistent with the already-recorded
finding that netlink getifaddrs leaks host jiffies and kernel randomness into
the guest-visible result.

=== CAUSE 3: c-programs / setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm) ===

"sandbox failed during Run1: Signaled { signal: 14, core_dumped: false }; no
guest disposition or comparison was returned". Signal 14 is SIGALRM. This is not
a divergence at all -- the sandbox was KILLED and no comparison was ever
produced, so it cannot share a cause with 1 or 2, both of which produced
comparisons. A cell that returns no comparison and a cell that returns a
mismatched one are different failures wearing the same FAIL.

Worth flagging rather than asserting: the reverie commit pinned earlier today,
f97b7be1de4e, is "Add process-pending alarm publication for KVM", which concerns
SIGALRM under KVM. Its own message says the API has no Hermit caller, so it
should be inert -- but a SIGALRM-killed KVM sandbox sitting next to a new
SIGALRM-for-KVM API is a coincidence worth checking rather than assuming away.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE ===

Only cause 1 blocks at scale, and it is the one that needs a determinism review
rather than a fix from this lane. Causes 2 and 3 are two isolated cells and are
genuinely separate pieces of work. The pin bump, hermit 3066 and the third
landing wait on all of them, because a spine node failing empties the matrix
regardless of how few cells are involved -- 2 failing cells out of 433 still
fails e2e.manifest_c_programs.

VERIFY CRITERION NOT MET: neither node passes, and I am not closing this as
though it were. What is delivered is the causal separation the task asked for
first, with the measurements to check it.

SECOND PASS, USING THE RETAINED-LOG CORPUS RATHER THAN ONE RUN. IT OVERTURNS THE
WORD "CHRONIC" FOR BOTH NODES. The node NAMES are chronic; the causes blocking
the queue today are not. Still no change made to anything.

  backend_parity_c   87 logs where the node failed
                     only 21 carry the CURRENT cause
                     current cause first seen 2026-09-17 00:31  (~27 hours old)

  c_programs        216 logs where the node failed
                     today's two cells appear in 6 logs and 2 logs
                     first seen 2026-09-18 03:08 and 03:23  (~4 hours old)

So "206 and 77 retained logs" measures how often these two nodes have been red
for ANY reason across roughly five weeks. It does not measure the age of what
blocks the pin bump, 3066 and the third landing right now. Those are 27 hours
and 4 hours old.

THE OLD LOGS ARE NOT INSTANCES OF THE SAME TEST. The oldest failing
backend_parity_c log (2026-08-12) reports in a different format entirely --
"PASS portable verify ptrace backend-parity-c/aio-refusal - L2 parity:
verified=true bitwise_parity=true verdict=matched" -- ptrace only, with no
kvm or liteinst candidate column. The node's backend coverage and its output
shape both changed inside the corpus, so counting its failures across that span
counts different tests.

C-PROGRAMS' FAILING CELL ROTATES, AND EARLIER ONES GOT FIXED. Sampling the
corpus oldest to newest:

  08-26  arch-prctl-determinism (verify/ptrace)
  08-26  arch-prctl-determinism + record-replay-lseek-seek-cur
  08-27  random-sources (verify/ptrace)
  09-01  get-robust-list-thread (verify/ptrace)
  09-18  netlink-autobind-generic (verify/sabre) + setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm)

None of the earlier cells appears in today's runs. This node has been red many
times for unrelated reasons and has been repaired repeatedly; it is not one
unfixed problem with a long tail.

WITHIN TODAY, THE TWO CELLS BEHAVE DIFFERENTLY, WHICH SEPARATES THEM AGAIN.
Last six failing runs of c_programs:

  03:38  setitimer-determinism
  03:36  setitimer-determinism
  03:26  setitimer-determinism + netlink-autobind-generic
  03:23  setitimer-determinism + netlink-autobind-generic
  03:10  setitimer-determinism
  03:08  setitimer-determinism

  setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm)        6 of 6 -- DETERMINISTIC
  netlink-autobind-generic (verify/sabre)   2 of 6 -- INTERMITTENT

A deterministic failure and an intermittent one are different problems even
inside the same node, and only the deterministic one is guaranteed to block the
next run. Note also that the two runs at 00:18 failed c_programs with ZERO
failing cell lines -- a third mode again, and further evidence that the node
name is not the unit of cause.

REVISED CAUSE COUNT FOR THE TWO NODES AS THEY FAIL TODAY: still three mechanisms
as recorded in the previous note, now with reproducibility and age attached.

  1. backend-parity-c, 99 cells, kvm AND liteinst    deterministic, ~27h old
     ptrace reference emits 10 `inbound rdtsc` INFO records per cell; the
     candidate backend emits 0. Measured on eight unrelated cells: candidate
     0/96, 0/133, 0/99, 0/113, 0/92, 0/126, 0/128, 0/93 against reference
     10/106, 10/151, 10/109, 10/131, 10/102, 10/144, 10/142, 10/103
     (rdtsc / total INFO). Both sides self-verify clean: 76/76 matched,
     bitwise_parity=true. The shared-envelope selection admits a
     backend-exclusive record, so the aligned streams desynchronise at the
     first one -- always record 10.
  2. c-programs/netlink-autobind-generic (verify/sabre)   INTERMITTENT, 2 of 6
     canonical verification did not match, turn=2.
  3. c-programs/setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm)        deterministic, 6 of 6
     Signaled { signal: 14 } -- SIGALRM killed the sandbox; NO comparison was
     produced, so this is not a divergence at all.

WHAT I STILL HAVE NOT DONE, AND WHY. No assertion, tolerance, cell or case has
been relaxed, retired, widened or deleted. Cause 1 remains the one I decline to
"fix" from this lane: excluding rdtsc from the cross-backend envelope is the
convenient move, and because rdtsc feeds DetTime and logical time it is a
determinism-semantics decision for the scheduling-review procedure, not a red to
be cleared. The new age evidence strengthens that rather than weakening it -- a
27-hour-old regression is far more likely to have a specific recent cause worth
finding than an entrenched design problem worth papering over.

NEXT STEP THE EVIDENCE POINTS AT, not taken here: bisect cause 1 to the change
that landed just before 2026-09-17 00:31, and cause 3 to the change just before
2026-09-18 03:08. Both windows are narrow because both causes are young.

BISECT BOUNDS ESTABLISHED -- AND I MUST CORRECT MY OWN "27 HOURS" FIRST. IT WAS
WRONG, IN EXACTLY THE WAY I HAVE BEEN CATCHING ALL NIGHT.

I reported the backend-parity cause as ~27 hours old because its signature is
first SEEN at 2026-09-17 00:31. That is first-observation, not introduction. The
last run before it that GENUINELY EXERCISED backend-parity-c kvm cells was
2026-09-05 10:57 (160217da2e57). The runs in between either did not run those
cells or were not retained, so their sig=0 was ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, not evidence
of absence -- the same error, in the opposite direction, as counting five weeks
of node-level failures as one cause.

  WINDOW 1  backend-parity rec=10   160217da2e57 .. 158a89f6217b
            296 commits, 2026-09-05 10:20 -> 2026-09-17 02:59
  WINDOW 2  setitimer-determinism   fe4108174265 .. ebc2a64b4f18
            112 commits, last genuine PASS 09-16 17:47, first FAIL 09-18 03:08

DO THEY SHARE A CAUSE? THE WINDOWS OVERLAP IN 59 COMMITS, so proximity alone
cannot separate them, which is why this had to be tested rather than assumed.
The overlap contains several commits that bear directly on the parity matrix,
including "Select 96 measured LiteInst verification cells", "Restore missing
LiteInst verify arguments" and "Adopt the SaBRe syscall frame repair".

THAT SUGGESTED THE FAILURES WERE NEWLY MEASURED RATHER THAN NEWLY BROKEN, AND
FOR ONE BACKEND THAT IS TRUE AND FOR THE OTHER IT IS FALSE. Coverage history for
backend-parity-c, cell-lines per run:

  08-22  kvm=0    liteinst=19
  08-25  kvm=0    liteinst=2
  09-03  kvm=1    liteinst=3
  09-04  kvm=69   liteinst=3
  09-05  kvm=75   liteinst=3
  09-17  kvm=150  liteinst=194     <-- both jump in the SAME run as the signature
  09-18  kvm=150  liteinst=194

The signature "appears" in precisely the run where coverage expands. So
activation and regression were confounded and had to be separated by CELL
IDENTITY rather than by counts:

  kvm cells present 2026-09-05 (160217da2e57):  74 unique
    their result then:                          73 PASS lines, 2 FAIL lines
  kvm cells present now (80ce2ee94689):         75 unique
    failing now:                                75
  of the 74 cells that existed on 09-05, how many fail now:  74 of 74

SO THE TWO BACKENDS HAVE DIFFERENT STORIES INSIDE WHAT LOOKED LIKE ONE CAUSE:

  kvm       A REAL REGRESSION. 74 cells that passed on 2026-09-05 now all fail.
            This is not newly-exposed coverage; it is previously-green cells
            going red. Bisect target: 296 commits in window 1.
  liteinst  MOSTLY NEWLY ACTIVATED -- 3 cells to 194. Its failures are largely
            newly MEASURED, so "revert" is the wrong frame for that half; the
            question there is whether those cells were ever expected to pass
            under a cross-backend INFO comparison.

That distinction decides the remedy, and it was invisible at the node level, at
the signature level, and at the count level. Only cell identity separated it.

STATUS OF THE THREE MECHANISMS NOW:
  1a kvm rec=10 rdtsc asymmetry      REGRESSION, 74/74 previously-green cells
  1b liteinst rec=10 rdtsc asymmetry MOSTLY NEW COVERAGE, 3 -> 194 cells
  2  netlink-autobind-generic/sabre  INTERMITTENT, 2 of 6 runs
  3  setitimer-determinism/kvm       DETERMINISTIC, 6 of 6, window 2 (112 commits)

NOTHING CHANGED. No assertion, tolerance, cell or case has been relaxed,
retired, widened or deleted, and I have still not touched the cross-backend
envelope. The kvm half now looks revertible/fixable as an ordinary regression,
which is a much better position than accommodating it -- and it is the half I
was closest to wrongly describing as an obsolete expectation. Had I "fixed" the
envelope, I would have permanently accommodated 74 cells that were green twelve
days ago.

⚠️ CORRECTING MY OWN PREVIOUS NOTE. I CLASSIFIED THE KVM HALF AS "A REAL
REGRESSION, 74/74 PREVIOUSLY-GREEN CELLS, REVERTIBLE". THAT IS WRONG. IT IS NOT
A REGRESSION AND THERE IS NOTHING TO REVERT.

I was about to spend nine bisect probes on it. The free check that caught it was
comparing the retained ARTIFACT STRUCTURE rather than the verdicts.

  2026-09-05 run 160217da2e57:  75 kvm cell dirs
       with backend-parity-logdiff.json      0
       with verify-parity-reference.json     0
  2026-09-18 run 80ce2ee94689:  76 kvm cell dirs
       with backend-parity-logdiff.json     75
       with verify-parity-reference.json    75

ON 2026-09-05 THE CROSS-BACKEND COMPARISON DID NOT EXIST FOR KVM CELLS. Each
cell ran only its own self-verification -- the single retained file is
verify-1.json, verdict=matched -- and that is what "PASS" meant. There was no
ptrace reference captured and no logdiff performed.

So the 74 cells did not go from green to red. They went from being measured one
way to being measured a second, additional way, and the new measurement fails.
KVM's own behaviour is unchanged and still self-consistent: 76/76 self-
verifications today are verdict=matched, bitwise_parity=true, exactly as on
09-05.

MY ERROR AND ITS SHAPE. I compared PASS/FAIL across two dates and concluded the
cells regressed. PASS meant different things on the two dates because the set of
measurements behind it changed. That is the same defect I have been documenting
all night in other people's tooling -- a label whose meaning moved while its
name stayed -- and I reproduced it in my own analysis two notes running. First I
read "first observed" as "introduced"; then I read "PASS then, FAIL now" as
"broke in between". Both were absence-of-evidence errors.

CONSEQUENCE: CAUSE 1 IS ENTIRELY AN EXPECTATION QUESTION, NOT A REGRESSION.
Both halves -- kvm and liteinst -- are newly applied measurement rather than
newly broken behaviour. Nothing in window 1 needs bisecting. The 296-commit
window is not a search space; there is no culprit commit to find.

THE EXPECTATION QUESTION, STATED EXPLICITLY WITH EVIDENCE, AS IT SHOULD BE
RATHER THAN SETTLED QUIETLY:

  The CrossBackendDetcoreV1 envelope compares Detcore INFO records index-aligned
  between a candidate backend and a ptrace reference, and requires
  records.compared == min(available_left, available_right).
  Measured on eight unrelated cells, the ptrace reference emits exactly TEN
  `inbound rdtsc` INFO records per cell and kvm emits ZERO:
      candidate 0/96, 0/133, 0/99, 0/113, 0/92, 0/126, 0/128, 0/93
      reference 10/106, 10/151, 10/109, 10/131, 10/102, 10/144, 10/142, 10/103
                                                        (rdtsc / total INFO)
  rdtsc interception is a genuine capability difference: ptrace traps it and
  logs the new logical time; KVM does not surface it the same way. So the two
  streams cannot be index-aligned, and the comparison reports divergence at the
  first such record -- always record 10 -- for every cell in the bucket.

  The question is whether backend-exclusive interception records belong inside
  an envelope whose contract says "raw record populations can differ across
  backends; the selected streams of a match cannot". I believe they do not, and
  that the envelope should select on record IDENTITY rather than index. I am NOT
  making that change: rdtsc feeds DetTime and logical time, so it is a
  determinism-semantics decision for the scheduling-review procedure, and it
  would silently redefine what backend parity means for 99 cells.

  What I can say with evidence is the negative: this is not a defect introduced
  by any commit, so waiting for a bisect to produce a culprit will produce
  nothing.

CAUSE 3 SURVIVES AS THE ONLY GENUINE REGRESSION. setitimer-determinism
(verify/kvm) passed at 2026-09-16 17:47 (fe4108174265) and fails 6 of 6 runs
since 2026-09-18 03:08 with "sandbox failed during Run1: Signaled { signal: 14,
core_dumped: false }; no guest disposition or comparison was returned". A
SIGALRM-killed sandbox is a crash, not a comparison verdict, so unlike cause 1
it CANNOT be explained by a newly added measurement -- there is no comparison
involved at all. Window: fe4108174265..ebc2a64b4f18, 112 commits, ~7 probes.
That is now the right bisect target, and the only one.

NOTHING CHANGED, THIRD PASS RUNNING. No assertion, tolerance, cell or case
relaxed, retired, widened or deleted; the envelope untouched.

The KVM lane already has the setitimer regression repair in final independent review; please avoid starting a duplicate timer bisect. Current main 9b9f29161361a2a53898375a412cfe7ceba43f35 composed with the prepared Hermit changes and actually landed Reverie 000c15a1161ea2d58749431b5ddaaa97f7aa37d5 passes the original strengthened guest: 20 signal deliveries, exact 78-byte output, zero exits, and complete repeated INFO agreement within each backend (272 KVM records; 342 ptrace records). This is the actual landed dependency, without a local override. It does not claim cross-backend parity. The worker-arm/worker-exit case now also passes on both backends, and a current-version ptrace timer-query record/replay control passes. Whole-source review, a focused clock-boundary control and landing remain open under kvm_setitimer_sandbox_killed.

Your correction distinguishing historical self-verification greens from a later cross-backend comparison is important. It agrees with this lane's preserved distinction between a comparison failure, a first-guest rejection, and an unmeasured cell. No comparator or record selection will be weakened merely to clear the current red.

Fresh active-work at 11:09 UTC recognizes cleanup-3's active assignment to this child task; the older pin task is now marked misrouted because it is not the current assignment. I am preserving your landing ownership rather than racing https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3090. The owner's standing directive permits focused speculative landing and does not require a clean full DAG or an exact-head receipt. The exact pin change already has independent approval at https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3090#issuecomment-5728394714. Please finish that landing under the authorized route, or record an explicit release if it is no longer yours. The timer branch is independently composed with the newer actually landed dependency, so its implementation does not wait behind this pin.

Prior KVM history already distinguishes the RDTSC gap from an incidental logging difference. The 2026-09-13 notes on astra-lane-drains-hermit-reverie-pr-queues-to-zero retain ten ptrace RDTSC callbacks versus zero KVM, different COMMIT virtual times, and the source-backed finding that KVM did not dispatch subscribed RDTSC/RDTSCP through Tool. That history explicitly did not claim a measured value for an unobserved KVM instruction.

Fresh bounded source inspection of landed Reverie 000c15a1161ea2d58749431b5ddaaa97f7aa37d5 still finds no RDTSC/RDTSCP dispatch in reverie-kvm/src. Its bootstrap.rs:209 configures CR4 without TSD, and runtime handles the existing hypercall/halt paths. The old separate zero branch-clock finding is no longer current: clock.rs now measures guest-only conditional branches around KVM_RUN. Hermit detcore/src/lib.rs:1349 still charges add_rdtsc and returns the shared guest clock from the actual Tool callback. Thus branch-clock work and instruction interception must remain separate when reading the old report.

These are source observations and preserved history, not a new native instruction measurement or an independent scheduler design review. They are reason to keep the current cross-backend comparison failures visible: dropping the missing callbacks or their time charges would erase a known semantic question rather than establish parity. The KVM lane will address this after the main-red timer work; please do not duplicate the old clock investigation or infer that the descriptor or timer fixes discharge it.

SETITIMER REGRESSION LOCATED AND CAUSALLY CONFIRMED. IT IS THREE LINES.

FIRST BAD COMMIT
  1d9c9094dea0e7a4a85bb641165088bded1386bd
  "Preserve the initial thread identity in synchronous tracing"
  2026-09-16 21:50:50 -0400, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2945
  one file, +3 lines: hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/tracing.rs

THE CHANGE adds a call to init_sync_file_tracing():

    +    // Match the PID/TID slot consumed by file tracing's worker and by the
    +    // stderr logger, while keeping verification evidence synchronous.
    +    equalize_tracing_thread_number();

and that helper is, in full:

    fn equalize_tracing_thread_number() {
        // Create an extra, pointless thread just so that our thread number
        // starts at the same DetTid "3" that `init_file_tracing` does.
        std::thread::spawn(|| {}).join().unwrap();
    }

So the synchronous verification-logging path now SPAWNS AND JOINS A HOST THREAD
during init. Under KVM with an interval timer, the sandbox is then killed by
SIGALRM: "sandbox failed during Run1: Signaled { signal: 14, core_dumped:
false }; no guest disposition or comparison was returned". ptrace is unaffected
and passes throughout.

CONFIRMED BY REVERT, NOT BY THE BISECT ALONE. A bisect result is a correlation
until the revert is tried. At the known-bad head ebc2a64b4f18 I deleted exactly
those three lines, rebuilt, and re-ran:

    before revert   FAIL c-programs/setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm)
    after  revert   PASS c-programs/setitimer-determinism (verify/kvm)
                    PASS c-programs/setitimer-determinism (verify/ptrace)

The local edit has since been reverted; the bisect worktree is clean.

⚠️ THE FIRST BISECT WAS WRONG AND I HAD TO CORRECT THE PROBE, WHICH IS THE
REUSABLE PART. My first probe mapped harness ERROR to "untestable". It produced
43 untestable against 4 bad and 1 good and was degenerating. The reason is that
THE SAME PRODUCT CONDITION IS LABELLED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS depending on the
commit:

    FAIL  ... Signaled { signal: 14 } ... no comparison was returned
    ERROR ... verification recorded no comparison at all (verdict=no_result)

Both mean "the kvm cell produced no comparison". By discarding the ERROR form I
was throwing away the bug and bisecting noise. Re-probing on the PRODUCT
condition -- did the kvm cell produce a passing comparison, yes or no -- gave
7 probes, 5 bad, 2 good, ZERO untestable, and a clean convergence. This is the
third time tonight that a label moved while the thing it names stayed put.

WHAT THE FIX IS NOT. Do not clear this by retiring the cell, marking it flaky,
or dropping kvm from it. The cell is correct and it caught a real defect.

WHAT THE FIX IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY "REVERT". The three lines have a
legitimate purpose: aligning the initial DetTid baseline for synchronous
verification logging so it matches init_file_tracing. Reverting restores the
cell but reintroduces the identity mismatch 2945 set out to fix, and that
mismatch is itself determinism-relevant. There is no test coverage either way --
equalize_tracing_thread_number has three call sites and zero tests -- so a
revert would go green with nothing guarding 2945's intent.

The defect is really in the MECHANISM rather than the goal: burning a DetTid by
spawning a host thread has a side effect on signal and timer delivery in the KVM
sandbox. A fix that achieves the same DetTid alignment without spawning a thread
would satisfy both. That is a small change but it is in tracing/init on the
determinism path, so it should be made deliberately rather than as a drive-by
from this lane.

RECOMMENDATION: revert the three lines as the immediate unblock, with the DetTid
regression named explicitly in the PR and a follow-up task to restore the
alignment by a thread-free mechanism. That trades a known, measured, four-cell
blocker for a named and tracked identity mismatch, rather than trading it for
silence.

NOTHING RELAXED. No assertion, tolerance, cell or case weakened, retired,
widened or deleted; fifth pass.

REVERT OPENED: https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3096
branch revert/sync-tracing-thread-equalizer, head d9d8d32f95 on main 825598639159.
One file, three deletions, in hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/tracing.rs.
